review.summary: This round reviews the post-merge follow-up from the task's Git Blame section, branch chore/TASK-066B-blame-ignore-revs, which starts from the TASK-066B squash commit on main. The squash commit c70d0c1 (#104) is on origin/main, and its tree is identical to the branch head reviewed in round 2. The change adds only a root .git-blame-ignore-revs and a CONTRIBUTING.md paragraph. The ignore file has one comment line naming TASK-066B and the squash commit's full 40-character SHA, in the format Git and GitHub accept. With the file, git blame on a reformatted PredictionsTab.tsx line reports the earlier commit instead of the squash commit. CONTRIBUTING.md documents the local blame.ignoreRevsFile opt-in as the task requires. The review-record validator passed. No frontend, CI or dependency change and no out-of-scope change was found; the one finding is a low-severity wording issue.

findings.summary: The new CONTRIBUTING.md paragraph says .git-blame-ignore-revs lists only formatting commits, but the listed TASK-066B squash commit also contains CI, Makefile, documentation and review-record changes that blame now skips as well.
findings.rationale: The task accepts that blame skips those non-formatting lines, but the paragraph implies every ignored line is a pure whitespace change. A reader tracing the format-check CI step, the Make targets or the documentation lines would not know why blame attributes them to an older commit.
findings.recommendation: Reword the paragraph to say the file lists commits that are mostly mechanical formatting, and note that the TASK-066B squash commit also contains its CI, Makefile and documentation lines, which blame skips too.
